result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.multi_source_shortest_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a shortest path to every node from whichever source is nearest. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L34845-L34932){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.multi_source_shortest_path( sources, cutoff=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Multi-source shortest paths](/assets/graphs/multi-source-shortest-path.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A two-by-four ladder with sources A and G. Each node is reached from whichever source is nearer, which splits the graph into two catchment areas: A serves B and E (accent color), G serves C, D, F, and H (teal). The shortest-path tree edges take their catchment's color, and each source has a halo. The card lists each catchment and the path to D, [G, C, D]." width="100%"} Runs one search that starts from all `sources=` at once, as if they were a single node. Each reachable node gets a shortest path from the source closest to it, so the result splits the graph into *catchment areas* (a graph Voronoi partition): read `path[0]` to see which source serves a node. Typical uses are nearest-facility questions: the closest hospital to every neighborhood, the nearest server to every client, or the closest seed gene to every protein in a network. "Shortest" follows the same rule as `shortest_path()`: fewest hops on an unweighted graph, lowest total weight (Dijkstra's algorithm) on a weighted graph. Directed graphs are followed in edge direction. When two sources are equally close, one is chosen. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. At least one is required. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Only return paths whose length is at most this value. If `None` (default), there is no limit. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Maps each reachable node ID to a shortest path (a list of node IDs) that starts at its nearest source. Each source maps to a one-node path. Unreachable nodes are absent. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `sources=` is empty or contains an ID or label that does not exist, or a weighted graph has a negative edge weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} With sources at both ends of a path, each node is served from the nearer end: ::: {#10faeb53 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F")]) ) paths = graph.multi_source_shortest_path(["A", "F"]) label = graph.get_label_from_id {label(t): [label(n) for n in p] for t, p in sorted(paths.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': ['A'], 'B': ['A', 'B'], 'C': ['A', 'B', 'C'], 'D': ['F', 'E', 'D'], 'E': ['F', 'E'], 'F': ['F']} ``` ::: ::: The first node of each path is the nearest source, which gives each node's catchment: ::: {#8f429ba3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} {label(t): label(p[0]) for t, p in sorted(paths.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'A': 'A', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'F', 'E': 'F', 'F': 'F'} ``` ::: :::
